feature: Fifty tracks and a hundred clips, fifth pass
summary: Adding a track or a clip to a 50 track edit while it plays, and taking it back, now fits in one 60 Hz frame. Every edit measured is 10 to 14 ms.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed. Your copy of the 50 track edit: File > Open (Cmd-Shift-G) ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev/Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz. Measured in the probe with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --wide 50 and --wide 100; numbers in Scripts/perf/baselines/wide-50.json and wide-100.json.

try.do: Open Reference Edit 50 tracks.photonz with File > Open.
Click + at the foot of the tracks and choose Video Track.
Double-click the new track's name, type a name and press Return.
While it plays, drag a recording in from the Library onto a track of its own.

evaluate: Does the picture keep playing smoothly as the track comes in?
Does the new track appear at once, with nothing flashing?
Does your own edit that lagged feel smooth now?
rough: Longest main thread hold, 50 tracks, last pass / now (bar 16 ms), worse of two full runs: add track 25.2 / 14.3, its undo 14.4 / 13.5, add clip 16.3 / 13.3, move 12.3 / 12.2, trim 9.4 / 10.8, pick 14.1 / 14.0, blade 13.0 / 13.9, undo of the blade 9.6 / 12.2.

Scrolling and zooming, main thread a frame, worse of the same two runs (bar p95 8.3): zoom in p95 7.4, out 6.9, near Fit 6.9, along 6.0, tracks down 4.8. One frame near Fit read 20.5 ms (bar none over 16). The one I caught was 21.9 ms, nearly all of it the main thread waiting inside the system's own drawing library.
Played end to end: 0 and 1 of 3637 frames dropped in the two runs, no clip frame wrong with ten up. Starting play at 0:58 from rest still waits about 728 ms.
An added empty track is bare room for two to four frames before its name and lane are drawn. Read from the timings, not filmed: the film step cannot add a track.
When a clip with sound comes or goes, the tracks under it take their new sound colour about a tenth of a second later.
For 0.4 seconds after an edit to an edit of more than 24 tracks, the window cannot be dragged by its title bar.
100 tracks has no bar: edits 14 to 23 ms, tracks down p95 17, 6 of 3639 frames dropped, 11 clip frames from ahead at 1:06.
Export not compared again: nothing in this pass touches drawing the picture. Nothing new was filmed; the film of zoom and scroll is in the fourth pass's report.
No mock covers a 50 track timeline.
